answer: A farm's five hundred clones all think the same thoughts, and that sameness is what to price against. Each epoch, agents commit claim hashes; payouts are set by each claim's information novelty, measured by semantic distance against the epoch's committed ledger. Near-duplicates merge into one pot split among them, so a clone army whispering the same line earns once while paying full cost per head. Tending the ledger is like tending a garden: reward what is new, and let the raven of redundancy pick dead copies clean. Parallelism stops paying, so the attack collapses on its own arithmetic.
